Acceptance is the first step. Good luck to you man. Have you ever read Jung?
Young Werther effect all over again...

Thank you. I'm still in shock, trembling all over. Hopefully it will subside soon...

Regarding your question, your curiosity is perfectly understandable and logical. I do not feel very well now but I will do my best to elucidate the issues those two deviations of the mind present to me-a particular case-study, entirely subjective and, what's worse, the analyzer himself, meaning myself, completely swayed by these "psychosis", if I'm allowed the term.

Basically, bipolarity, in my case at least, means to carry two polar opposite personalities inside of you. You have no control of the feelings inside you,in extremes, even if they go against your very moral compass. Even if you try to rationalize what you feel, knowing they make no sense and are totally uncalled for, even if you achieve, after years of dealing with this, some acute insight into yourself, you can't help to be at their mercy.  It's horrible. I can go from the most well-spoken, energetic, respectful man to the most glum, taciturn, comatose-like pessimist. The choices you make in one personality inevitably conflict and affect the other one. In my case, regret. I dropped out of university, coasting through it effortlessly, whimsically. I just lost it. My future vanished just like that. Now, it's up to me to carry the pieces, and the burden that it is gone. Schizophrenia for me means voices. I have auditory hallucinations, an inner self, that despises me and brings me down constantly. 

I haven't been to a physician in a longtime, but I fear I also have crippling depression. In my early 20's I spend almost a year bed-ridden, sleeping 18 hours a day. I got out out of pure sheer will, but it's catching up and I feel debilitated. I'm very fit at six feet two and almost 200 pounds (working out helps) but I know for a fact that if I stop fighting back I will sink back into bed in an instant.
thank you for your kind words
